title: Regulated Degradation Controller with Grace Periods and Trickle Recovery
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During region-level overloads and gradual capacity degradation we currently apply blunt shedding policies (static token buckets or simple priority lanes) that cause sharp drops in availability for mid-tier customers and instability when traffic rebounds. We need a controller that implements more regulated degradation: preserve high-priority latency SLOs, avoid cascading failures during multi-region failover, and enable graceful re-introduction of load (trickle recovery) without causing thundering herd.

Goals:
- Implement a Regulated Degradation Controller (RDC) that centralizes admission policies across priority lanes, per-tenant credit balances, and region spillover coordination.
- Provide a short-term grace period for in-flight and recently-active sessions to avoid immediate eviction of requests that would cause poor UX (e.g., streaming chat).
- Support trickle recovery: a controlled ramp of accepted traffic after enforced shedding to stabilize caches/KV warmups and downstream systems.
- Make degradation modes observable and actionable: expose per-tenant metrics, reason codes, and suggested remediation (retry-after / fallback hints).
- Ensure deterministic behavior during multi-region failover: when primary region degrades, downstream agents can accept limited spillover with fidelity downgrade rather than full rejection.

High-level design:
1) Admission policy core: policy evaluates requests by (priority, tenant_credit_balance, deadline, region_affinity, last_activity_age). It returns an admission decision: ACCEPT, ACCEPT_GRACE, THROTTLE_TRICKLE, PARTIAL_ACCEPT, REJECT.
2) Grace periods: short-lived tokens (default 3s) assigned when a session sends steady streaming traffic or has a recent successful admission; requests within the token window get ACCEPT_GRACE to avoid dropping a live stream. Grace window configurable per-priority.
3) Tenant credit ledger: tenants accumulate credits when idle (configurable accrual rate) up to a cap; credits can be spent during bursts to avoid immediate rejection. Credits decay on a long time constant to prevent hoarding. Metric: shedding.per_tenant.credit_balance.
4) Trickle recovery state machine: after shedding a lane/region, the RDC transitions to TRICKLE state for a controlled duration, emitting rate-limited admits (configurable tokens/sec) and monitoring success metrics (latency, error-rate). If metrics improve for the observation window, increase rate; if regress, revert to shed.
5) Deadline-aware preemption: when necessary, the controller can switch ACCEPT -> PARTIAL_ACCEPT which returns a structured partial response (structured output with fallback flag) and a token-preserving hint for client retry. Provides an intermediate fidelity instead of 429.
6) Multi-region coordination: region controllers publish compact state (regional_load_score, spillover_budget) to a regional orchestrator. During failover, inbound tokens are admitted only if spillover_budget > 0 and with reduced fidelity tag.
7) Circuit-breaker integration: each lane has an upstream circuit meter; repeated rejections open fast-fail path and increase trickle damping to prevent oscillation.

API/Behavioral contract changes:
- New response headers: X-Redwood-Degradation-Mode: OFF|GRACE|TRICKLE|PARTIAL|REJECTED; X-Redwood-Trace-Reason: short code; Retry-After or Retry-Tokens header when applicable.
- New 206-style partial success semantics for generation endpoints (Partial-OK) documented in API spec.

Observability and SLOs:
- New metrics: shedding.controller.rejections, shedding.controller.grace_accepts, shedding.controller.trickle_recovery_rate, shedding.per_tenant.credit_balance, shedding.controller.partial_accepts, region.failover.spillover_rate.
- SLOs impacted: latency.p95 and availability for P0/P1 customers. Add dashboards showing per-region shed ratio and correlation with KV cache hit-rate during trickle windows.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag gated behind runtime flag: rdc_v1_enabled.
- Staging: enable for 5 internal tenants, run 48h load tests with synthetic spike.
- Canary: enable in us-east-1 for 2% of traffic with canary metrics alarm: >5% increase in p95 or >2x rejections logs triggers rollback.
- Gradual ramp and observability validation before global flip.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for enrolment/aging/credit arithmetic and state transitions.
- Integration tests with region orchestrator simulation that injects failover and verifies spillover budgets and fidelity tags.
- Chaos test: run a 3-minute degraded node scenario to ensure trickle recovery stabilizes within 5x window.

Docs and runbooks:
- Add operator runbook: how to force-enter TRICKLE, how to drain grace tokens, and emergency cutoff commands.
- User-facing docs: explain new headers and Partial-OK semantics to SDK teams.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs predictability: credit ledger and trickle state machine add complexity but significantly reduce thrash and improve user experience.
- Partial responses increase SDK complexity; but preferred over 429 in streaming/chat UX.
- Global coordination increases latency in decision path; we keep admissions region-local with periodic regional budgets to avoid synchronous global calls.
acceptance_criteria:
1) RDC can be feature-flag toggled and does not change default behavior when off.
2) Grace window correctly allows in-flight streams to finish (tests simulate streaming sessions).
3) Tenants can spend accrued credits during bursts and audit shows credit accounting matches expected accrual/decay.
4) Trickle recovery stabilizes cache hits and reduces downstream errors compared to immediate full acceptance.
5) New metrics emitted and dashboard panels populate during staging canary.
6) Documentation updated and SDKs receive Partial-OK handling docs.
implementation_notes:
- Implement ledger as a sharded in-memory store with optional Redis fallback for persisted balances.
- Admission core must be cheap: decision path should be <200us median. Use precomputed policy table keyed by (priority, region_level).
- Grace tokens attached to session metadata; streaming clients receive Grace TTL in initial accept.
- Partial-OK uses a small structured envelope: {status: 'partial', reason_code: 'TRIM_DEADLINE', truncated_tokens: N, fallback_hint: URL}. SDKs should parse and surface to app.
- Backpressure hooks: tie trickle admit rate to KV cache warmup metric to ensure downstream readiness.
- Include feature toggle to disable tenant credit spend in emergency mode.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Primary alerts:
- P0: shedding.controller.rejections_rate > baseline by 3x for 10m AND p95_latency increase > 25% -> paging SRE.
- Trickle-failure: trickle_recovery_failure_count > 5 in 15m -> investigate cache priming.
- Credit-imbalance: any tenant credit_balance > cap for 24h -> notify billing/team.
Dashboards: per-region shed ratio, per-tenant credit balance heatmap, trickle state transitions timeline, partial_accept repartition by route.
rollback_plan:
- Flip rdc_v1_enabled off via runtime feature flag.
- Fallback to legacy token-bucket admission.
- If partial responses created client-side issues, set header gating to always REJECT instead of PARTIAL for canary.
- Post-rollback: run analysis on logs to find root cause and disable specific subcomponents (grace, trickle, credits) independently.
comments: 2026-01-11 - Maya Chen: Initial proposal posted. Focus on minimizing SRE toil and preserving streaming UX. Requested review from runtime and console owners.

2026-01-14 - Design review (Lena Müller): Asked for clarity on credit accrual math and edge-case when tenant uses credits over multiple regions. Action: add decay and per-region cap in the ledger design.

2026-01-18 - Arjun Patel: Prototype ledger implemented in-memory with sharding by tenant hash. Observed median decision latency 120us in local bench; need to optimize serialization path for header tags.

2026-01-22 - QA (Diego Alvarez): Integration tests added to simulate failover; discovered race where grace tokens persisted across region failover causing cross-region affinity issues. Fix: grace tokens are bounded to origin region and evicted on failover event.

2026-01-28 - Security (Priya Rao): Reviewed API header surface; no sensitive data exposed. Recommended telemetry sampling for credit balances to avoid PII-like leak — implemented sampling at 1% by default.

2026-02-01 - Performance (Jamal Reed): Canary in us-east-1 (2% traffic) ran for 12h. Observed 18% reduction in hard rejections and improved p95 for P1 tenants during spikes. Noted minor increase in avg decision latency (+8ms tail) — optimizing policy cache next.

2026-02-02 - Arjun Patel: Moving to broader canary after policy cache optimization (ENG-381208 created for policy cache work). Next steps: update SDK docs for Partial-OK and schedule runbook walk-through with SREs.
2026-02-02 - Product (Nina Park): Approved canary expansion contingent on no customer-facing errors and updated docs. Tracked as release blocker for runtime-1.22.
notes_for_follow_up:
